🎙 Enemies moved from ‘unconditional surrender’ to ‘unconditional negotiations’: Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says the US and Israeli regime failed to achieve their objectives in the two recent wars against Iran, shifting from demands for “unconditional surrender” to “unconditional ceasefire” in the 12-day war and “unconditional negotiations” in the 40-day war.

Speaking in a meeting on Monday, Araghchi said the past two years have been marked by intense pressure from the United States and the Israeli regime, two wars, economic sanctions, assassinations, and domestic conspiracies, adding that the adversaries had used all their capabilities to undermine Iran.
​
Referring to the outcomes of the two wars of aggression, the top Iranian diplomat said that after 12 days of fighting, the enemies had moved from demanding Iran’s “unconditional surrender” to seeking an “unconditional ceasefire.”
​
In the 40-day war, he added, they shifted after about 20 days from calls for “unconditional surrender” to “unconditional negotiations” and efforts to reach an agreement through diplomacy. He noted that the confrontation has not entirely ended and that the government, Armed Forces, state officials and Iranian people have all been involved.
​
Pointing to the military might of the United States and the Israeli regime, as well as the political and military support they received from some European and regional countries, Araghchi said that despite these capabilities and backing, the aggressors have failed to achieve their goals against the Iranian people.
​
He described resistance as the key to Iran’s victories over the past 47 years, particularly during the past two years, stressing that preventing the enemy from achieving its objectives constitutes a victory for Iran.
​
Elsewhere in his remarks, Araghchi outlined the Foreign Ministry’s responsibilities in wartime, including defending Iran’s positions in international forums, conveying the Iranian people’s voice to the world, and pursuing diplomatic solutions to lift sanctions.
​
The top Iranian diplomat stressed that, alongside keeping the path of negotiations open, the Foreign Ministry must help strengthen the country’s resilience against pressure and sanctions.
​
Araghchi said the ministry must identify alternative supply routes, find new markets, and expand exports to mitigate the impact of sanctions, sustain production, and preserve employment.
​
He described provincial diplomacy as an important tool in achieving these goals, saying provincial offices should shift their focus from primarily consular affairs to identifying and activating the economic capacities of their provinces and expanding ties with provinces in neighboring and other countries.
​
Emphasizing the importance of economic diplomacy in strengthening the country’s economic independence, Araghchi called on all Foreign Ministry officials to identify opportunities, increase their efforts, expand exports, and help the country overcome its current circumstances.

On the ground, the Houthis are pressing an offensive in Lahj province. Analysts at the Critical Threats Project and the Institute for the Study of War assessed that it aims to sever the supply route between Mokha and Aden and isolate government-aligned forces on the Red Sea coast.

Riyadh has to defend its allies’ supply lines and its own airspace. The Houthis get to threaten both, then announce which places the war should spare.
